thread:
mira: Heads up — ~15% p95 latency spike for a private/VPC deployment (acme-prod) started ~11:12 UTC. Users report tail latency and a few 502s. Anyone seeing alerts?

infra-bot: [ALERT] acme-prod egress latency anomaly (p95 +14%) at 2025-11-15T11:12:04Z — metrics: https://metrics/redwood/acme-prod/egress

jonathan: I pulled a flamegraph around 11:10-11:20. Kernel selector fell back to the generic (fallback) path for a subset of requests and we see heavy memcpy/serialize time in the kv kernel. This correlates with the batching heuristics change we rolled at 11:05. Snippet from perf report:

```
11:12:10 - kernel: kv_fast_path_v2 -> 20%
11:12:10 - kernel: kv_generic_memcpy -> 38%
11:12:11 - user: batching_coordinator::open_conn -> 25%
```

alex: On infra side, NAT/SNAT pool on the customer's private egress showed port exhaustion spikes at the same time. conntrack entries spiked and ephemeral port pool was saturated. excerpts: 

```
conntrack: entries 98234 -> 288172 (limit 300k)
ss -s: TCP: established 1200, timewait 48000, orphaned 0
SNAT port range used: 1000/1024
```

lina: Firewall logs also show lots of fragmentation / MSS-clamp events outbound. I see PMTU blackhole patterns and iptables mss-clamp at 1420 on the NAT box, but backend workers were using 1500. Might be causing retransmits and extra connection churn.

jonathan: Root cause hypothesis: the new batching heuristic reduced internal request coalescing and caused the runtime to open many short-lived outbound connections per token-stream (we accidentally set connection reuse to `off` for streaming). Without keepalive and with a small SNAT port pool, each short TCP -> new SNAT port -> TIME_WAIT backlog. Combined with kernel selector fallback (less efficient kernel), per-request latency jumped. Example header we observed on worker: 

```http
POST /model/gen HTTP/1.1
Host: model-host
Connection: close
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
```

mira: Customer is on a private deployment with default SNAT pool (1024 ports) and strict firewall MTU rules. Can infra route them through a dedicated egress IP/pool while we mitigate?

alex: Yes. Mitigation plan: 1) revert batching heuristic to yesterday's config (already staged), 2) enable TCP keepalive and connection pooling on runtime workers, 3) temporarily increase conntrack & SNAT port pool for acme-prod, 4) route acme-prod through dedicated NAT with larger port range, 5) follow up on MTU/mss-clamp. I'll start the NAT change and bump conntrack timeouts.

ops-bot: Deploy triggered: revert-batcher @eng-runtime — rolling restart of 5 runtime nodes (started 11:23 UTC).

jonathan: After revert + enabling keepalive on the runtime workers, conntrack usage dropped from ~98% -> ~15% within ~3 minutes and p95 returned to baseline. Quick numbers: p95 before fix 420ms, peak 610ms, after mitigation 430ms -> baseline ~410ms. No more 502s being reported.

lina: Filed infra ticket INFRA-2248 (MTU/firwall/RFC) to audit path MTU, adjust mss-clamp rules, and add PMTU logs for private deployments. I'll own the follow-up. :clipboard:

sre-oncall: Will add an alert for SNAT pool saturation + correlate with batching config changes so this doesn't regress silently.

mira: Thanks — great catch. Action items: jonathan/eng-runtime to add a guard in the batching rollout (automated canary + SNAT-sensitivity check), alex/infra to finish dedicated egress route and update runbook for SNAT sizing, lina to finish INFRA-2248 and link postmortem. Please paste the postmortem here when ready.

jonathan: I'll add the profiling artifacts and a short RCA doc to the postmortem. Also updating the runtime config defaults to enable keepalive for streaming clients.

mira: Closing thread for now, reopen if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
